verdict: Google is spending without converting; leads dropped 40% this week.
narrative: In the last 28 days, you received 30 leads at an average cost of $125.91 per lead — every one of them came from Meta, while Google Ads spent $2,080.23 and produced zero conversions. That imbalance drove a 54.61% spike in cost per lead week-over-week and a 40% drop in lead volume, with the most recent three days showing that trend worsening, not leveling off. Google Ads is being audited now to identify whether the issue is conversion tracking, bid strategy, or campaign structure, and spend is being scrutinized against that zero-return result. On the pipeline side, 30 leads entered your system this period but none have progressed to appointments, which points to an intake or routing gap that is being addressed separately from the ads. Next period, the goal is to restore Google to measurable performance or reallocate that budget to what is working, and to get leads moving through the pipeline once they arrive.

watch_item.issue: Google Ads is consuming the majority of paid budget with zero conversions recorded over 28 days, and the lead decline is accelerating.
watch_item.fix: A full audit of Google Ads conversion tracking and bid strategy is underway now, with budget decisions to follow the findings.
